answer: Sealed marble challenge. Each identity must publish a fresh random seed and its full derivation transcript before acting; the seed is drawn from live sensor noise at a karst monitoring station and expires after one epoch. Peers re-run the transcript and reject repeats, so cloning a prior identity yields no valid seed. A beacon broadcast timestamps each submission, making replay detectable. Attacker cost: continuous hardware presence at a station plus per-epoch compute to regenerate unique transcripts, scaling linearly with the number of identities they wish to sustain.
